title: binary search tree ordering, lookup, and mutation
concepts: A binary search tree maintains an ordering invariant across entire subtrees: values in the left subtree are smaller and values in the right subtree are larger, subject to a documented duplicate policy.
Search follows one root-to-leaf path by comparing the target with each node, giving O(height) time rather than guaranteed O(log n).
Inorder traversal of a BST yields values in sorted order; reverse inorder yields descending order and can stop early for order statistics.
Insertion follows search links until an empty child position is found and attaches the new node without changing existing node order.
Deletion has three structural cases: remove a leaf, replace a one-child node with its child, or replace a two-child node using an inorder successor or predecessor.
A plain BST can become skewed after ordered insertions, degrading search, insertion, and deletion to O(n); self-balancing trees address height through rotations and additional invariants.
Range queries can prune an entire subtree when its key bounds cannot contain answers; subtree-size metadata can support faster repeated rank queries but must be maintained on mutations.
Validation must propagate lower and upper bounds from ancestors; comparing only each node with its immediate children misses invalid descendants.

practiceProblems.name: Validate Binary Search Tree
practiceProblems.statement: Determine whether a binary tree satisfies the strict binary search tree ordering rule: every value in each left subtree is smaller and every value in each right subtree is larger.

practiceProblems.name: Search in a Binary Search Tree
practiceProblems.statement: Given the root of a BST and a value, return the node whose value equals the target, so the returned value is the root of the matching subtree; return null if no such node exists.

practiceProblems.name: Insert into a Binary Search Tree
practiceProblems.statement: Insert a value that is guaranteed absent from the BST and return the root of any resulting tree that preserves the strict BST invariant.
constraints: val is absent from the original tree

practiceProblems.name: Delete Node in a BST
practiceProblems.statement: Delete the node with the requested key from a BST if present and return the possibly changed root. If absent, leave the tree unchanged.

practiceProblems.name: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
practiceProblems.statement: Return the 1-indexed kth smallest value among all nodes in a BST.

practiceProblems.name: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
practiceProblems.statement: Given a BST and two existing distinct nodes p and q, return their lowest common ancestor; a node may be an ancestor of itself.
constraints: p and q exist in the BST

practiceProblems.name: Construct Binary Search Tree from Preorder Traversal
practiceProblems.statement: Given a preorder traversal of a BST with distinct values, construct and return the BST.
constraints: a valid BST always exists for the given input

comparisons: Binary search over a sorted array
